requirement_text.REQ-425:
MOB-6 in docs/mobile/requirements.md (build-order M6; depends on M2). Built BEFORE MOB-4 (REQ-426..428) -- see the S9 header: the renderers' six states classify this requirement's ApiError. SECURITY-REVIEWER gate (refresh-token handling, token clearing).

Hardens lib/api/api_client.dart (created by REQ-421) into the single client:
1. Attach the active tenant's bearer token (REQ-422's iss check).
2. On 401: exactly one silent refresh via flutter_appauth's token refresh, then exactly one retry of the original request; concurrent 401s share one in-flight refresh. On refresh failure: clear the tenant's tokens (REQ-422 store) and route to login.
3. Exponential backoff on 5xx for idempotent methods only (GET), bounded attempts; POST is not auto-retried (no duplicate task completion).
4. Normalise every failure to a sealed ApiError type before it leaves lib/api/: at minimum network-unavailable, unauthorized, forbidden (403), not-found, module-not-available (a 404 on any /api/v1/modules/<id>/ path -- architecture.md §6: absence is 404, not 403, and must not render as a generic not-found), backpressure (429, carrying the Retry-After seconds -- the backend emits 429 from lib/letflow/plugs/admission.ex and lib/letflow/plugs/public_read_rate_limit.ex), validation (422 with RFC 9457 field errors), conflict (409), server (5xx after retries).
5. A static guard (apps/mobile/test/guards/), the counterpart of the SPA's raw-fetch-outside-client guard in web/tests/guards/: no file outside lib/api/ imports package:dio or package:http or uses dart:io HttpClient; with a self-test.

task.description:
Design REQ-425 (MOB-6) before any implementation. Read apps/mobile/lib/api/api_client.dart, api.dart and transport_policy.dart FIRST -- this file already exists (created by REQ-419, extended by REQ-421's tenant-context wiring and REQ-422's on-device hardening/tenant-scoped audience checks) and this requirement hardens it further, it does not start from nothing. Read apps/mobile/test/api/api_client_test.dart for the existing test surface and apps/mobile/test/guards/forbidden_dependencies_guard_test.dart plus web/tests/guards/forbidlist.ts as the two existing static-guard precedents (one Dart-side, one TS-side) to model the new single-client guard on for consistency of shape.

Write lib/letflow/design/req425-mobile-api-client-hardening.md covering:
1. The sealed ApiError type -- exact variant list (network-unavailable, unauthorized, forbidden, not-found, module-not-available, backpressure(retryAfterSeconds), validation(fieldErrors per RFC 9457), conflict, server), and the exact mapping rule from status code/exception to variant, INCLUDING the module-404-vs-plain-404 path-matching rule against /api/v1/modules/<id>/ (state the exact path-matching regex/logic).
2. The 401-refresh-then-retry state machine: what mediates 'concurrent 401s share one in-flight refresh' (e.g. a single in-flight Future/completer the client holds), the exact sequence (attempt request -> 401 -> acquire-or-await shared refresh -> on success retry original request exactly once -> on failure clear tokens via REQ-422's store and route to login), and how a SECOND 401 on the retried request itself is handled (must not loop -- state the terminal behavior explicitly, this is an open question CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR will check for).
3. The 5xx backoff mechanism for GET only: the named bounded-attempts constant (name it, e.g. kMaxServerRetryAttempts, in lib/api/), the backoff delay formula (must be deterministic/testable under a fake clock -- state the exact formula, e.g. base * 2^attempt with a stated base and cap), and the exact non-retry rule for POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE.
4. The static single-client guard's design: what file(s) it scans, what import statements it flags (package:dio, package:http, dart:io HttpClient), what counts as 'outside lib/api/', and its self-test fixture shape (a fixture file under lib/features/ importing package:dio that the guard's OWN test asserts gets flagged, modeled on how forbidden_dependencies_guard_test.dart or web's forbidlist.ts self-tests today -- read whichever is closer in shape before choosing).
5. Function signatures with @spec-style type shapes for every new/changed public function in lib/api/ (the client's request methods, the ApiError type and its variants, the refresh coordinator, the guard's entry point) -- signatures and type shapes only, no implementation bodies.
6. Map every one of the 7 acceptance criteria (listed below) to a concrete design element. No acceptance criterion left unaddressed, no TBD/deferral language.
7. List open questions explicitly rather than silently resolving them by guessing (e.g. if flutter_appauth's refresh API shape is not already established by REQ-421/422's code, state that as an open question for MOBILE-DEV to resolve against the actual package API during implementation, rather than inventing a fictitious method name).

Complete the handoff: artifacts_out: ["lib/letflow/design/req425-mobile-api-client-hardening.md"], next_action: "Route to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (Step 1b)".
acceptance_criteria: a test where the fake server returns 401 once then 200 asserts exactly one refresh call and exactly one retry, and that two concurrent requests both receiving 401 trigger one refresh total
a test where refresh fails asserts the tenant's tokens are deleted from the secure store and the router is at the login route

a test asserts a GET receiving 503 twice then 200 succeeds with increasing delays between attempts (fake clock), a GET receiving 503 on every attempt stops after the maximum attempt count declared as a named constant in lib/api/ and surfaces ApiError server (the test asserts the exact number of requests sent), and a POST receiving 503 is not retried

a test per ApiError variant asserts the mapping from status code/exception, including 404 on /api/v1/modules/exam/x -> module-not-available, 404 elsewhere -> not-found, and 429 with 'Retry-After: 7' -> backpressure(7 seconds)
a test asserts no DioException or SocketException escapes lib/api/ -- the public client API returns or throws only ApiError
the single-client guard fails its self-test fixture (a file under lib/features/ importing package:dio) and passes on the real tree
cd apps/mobile && flutter analyze && flutter test pass, real output quoted, and SECURITY-REVIEWER signs off before merge

result.summary: Wrote lib/letflow/design/req425-mobile-api-client-hardening.md hardening apps/mobile/lib/api/api_client.dart per MOB-6. Covers: (1) sealed ApiError type with 9 variants (network-unavailable, unauthorized, forbidden, not-found, module-not-available(moduleId), backpressure(retryAfterSeconds), validation(fieldErrors), conflict, server) and the exact classifyError mapping rule including the /api/v1/modules/<id>/ regex (^/api/v1/modules/([^/]+)/) distinguishing module-404 from plain-404; (2) the 401 refresh-then-retry state machine via a _RefreshCoordinator holding a single in-flight Future (coalesces concurrent 401s), exact sequence attempt->401->refresh-or-join->retry-once, and an explicit terminal rule for a second 401 on the retried request itself (an extra.'_letflowRetriedAfter401' flag prevents a second refresh attempt -- surfaces UnauthorizedError and stops, no loop); (3) GET-only exponential backoff via named kMaxServerRetryAttempts=3 constant, formula kBaseServerRetryDelay*2^(attempt-1) capped at kMaxServerRetryDelay, with an injectable delayFn for fake-clock testing, and the exact POST non-retry rule; (4) the single-client guard design (checkSingleApiClientBoundary) modeled on token_storage_boundary_guard_test.dart's shape, flagging package:dio/package:http imports and dart:io HttpClient(...) construction outside lib/api/, with a self-test fixture under lib/features/; (5) full @spec-style signatures for ApiClient's new/changed methods, AppAuthAdapter.refresh, and every classifyError helper; (6) an acceptance-criteria resolution map covering all 7 criteria; (7) 8 open questions (OQ-1..OQ-8), most notably OQ-2 -- flutter_appauth ^12.1.0's actual refresh-token-grant method/type is not established anywhere in the existing codebase (only authorizeAndExchangeCode exists today) and is explicitly left for MOBILE-DEV to verify against the real package API rather than guessed at. No implementation code included -- signatures and type/field shapes only.
